ὑπαναγιγνώσκω.definition: read clause by clause, Is.11.4, Aeschin.2.109; Hyp.Eux.40; read aloud, Hierocl.in CA27p.484M

ὑπανάγω.definition: withdraw, J.AJ4.4.5; lead gradually back, is f.l. for in Hierocl.in CA15p.454M

ὑπαναδύομαι.definition: Med., withdraw secretly from, endeavour to escape, D.H.7.13: abs., Com.Adesp.19.3 D

ὑπανακαθαίρω.definition: purge gently, cj. for in Sor.1.86

ὑπανάκειμαι.definition: Pass., recline below at table, D.L.7.17

ὑπανακινέω.definition: intr., rise up and go away, Ar.Ec.1165

ὑπανακλάω.definition: bend up under, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.75

ὑπαναλίσκω.definition: waste away, spend or consume gradually; spend as a contribution, . . BMus.Inscr. 425

ὑπαναμιμνήσκομαι.definition: recall to mind once more, Aesop.157H

ὑπαναπείθω.definition: exert undue influence upon, Mitteis Chr.96 ii 11, cf. 18

ὑπαναπίμπλαμαι.definition: Pass., to be filled gradually, with . . , Ael.NA17.13

ὑπαναπλέω.definition: rise and float on the surface, Ph.1.320,565,593

ὑπανάστασις.definition: rising up from one's seat, Arist.EN1165a28, cf. Phld.Hom.p.36O.: pl., Pl.R.425b, Porph.Abst.2.61: cf. 2

ὑπαναφλέγομαι.definition: Pass., to be heated gradually, Ael.VH14.41

ὑπαναφύομαι.definition: grow or swell up under or gradually, ib.7, NA4.21

ὑπαναχωρέω.definition: go back gradually, retire slowly, Th.1.51; D.H.5.8, cf. S.E.M.9.293, D.C.63.26; of death, PMasp.151.37

ὑπανερπύζω.definition: creep up secretly or softly, Ael.NA5.3

ὑπανθέω.definition: begin to flower or blossom, Philostr.Im.1.31, Poll.1.60; Id.2.10

ὑπανιάομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat distressed, opt. Ar.Nu.1195

ὑπανίημι.definition: remit or relax a little; intr., Plu.Aem.23:—so in Pass., Ph.2.87, al

ὑπανίσταμαι.definition: Pass. with aor. 2 and pf. Act., rise; rise up from their seats to make room or show respect to . . , Hdt.2.80, cf. Phld.Vit.p.38J.; Ar.Nu.993 ; X.Lac.15.6; Id.Hier.7.2, cf. Smp.4.31; Id.Mem.2.3.16: metaph., gave way, …

ὑπανίσχω.definition: rise slowly, of the moon, Ael.NA11.10; Philostr.VA3.1

ὑπανοίγω.definition: or open from below, tap a cask; open underhand or secretly, D.32.28; Luc.Asin.13

ὑπαντάω.definition: Ion. APl.4.101: fut; meet, encounter, of a heavenly body, Ptol.Tetr.132

ὑπάντησις.definition: Astrol., encounter of a heavenly body, in Ptol.Tetr.132; metaph., retort, answer, S.E.M.11.202; ib.7.278, A.D.Synt.305.19

ὑπαντήτωρ.definition: heavenly body encountered in course of projection of vital quadrant, Heph.Astr.2.11.72.28), Doroth.inCat.Cod. Astr.2.198.15, Sch.Ptol.Tetr.169

ὑπαντιάζω.definition: come or go to meet, encounter, without case, Il.6.17, Pi.P.4.135, A.Pers.407, X.Cyr.4.2.18: c. dat., Pi.P.8.11, Pae.2.32, A.Pers.834,850, X.Cyr.5.5.9: also c. acc., Pi.P.5.44, Hdt.4.121, J.AJ1.10.4, Plu.Pomp.71, App.M…

ὑπαντιάω.definition: = foreg., only in Ep. part. Opp.H.2.565

ὑπάντομαι.definition: only in pres. and impf., = Hdn.4.11.2, 8.7.8

ὑπάπειμι.definition: withdraw, retreat, Th.5.9; withdraw stealthily, Id.3.111; Luc.Icar.14; . . was past the age of . . , Philostr.VA6.3

ὑπαποκινέω.definition: intr., move off secretly or softly, sneak away, c. gen., Ar.Av.1011

ὑπαπολείπομαι.definition: Pass., to be left behind , ib.10.43

ὑπαποτρέχω.definition: run away secretly, slip away, Ar.Ec.284

ὑπαράσσω.definition: Att. strike underneath, Anon. ap. Suid

ὑπαργυρεύω.definition: dub. sens., perh. use base money, Plu.2.832a

ὑπάργυρος.definition: having silver underneath: hence; of rocks and the like , containing silver, veined with silver, E.Cyc.294, Rh.970; X.Vect.1.5, 4.2: metaph. of men, containing a proportion of silver, Pl.R.415c; cf

ὑπαρόω.definition: plough just before sowing, Thphr.HP8.11.8, CP3.20.8

ὑπαρτάω.definition: hang or bind on underneath, Ael.NA5.7

ὑπαρχή.definition: not a vestige of an eye, IG42 .121.75; very freq. in the phrase from or in the beginning, Arist.Pol.1293a2, al.; Id.HA590a21

ὑπαρχιτέκτων.definition: deputy clerk of the works, IG22.1678aA7 , Delph.3.25 ii A 13 , PPetr.2p.138, al. , IG7.3073.160

ὑπαρχιφυλακίτης.definition: deputy chief of police, BGU1222.61, al

ὕπαρχος.definition: subordinate commander, lieutenant; subordinate governor, of satraps, etc., Hdt.3.70, 4.166, al., X.An.4.4.4; Th.8.31; Sor.Vit.Hippocr.8; in the Seleucid kingdom, OGI225.36

ὑπάρχω.definition: fut. Hdt.6.109, S.Ant.932 : aor; c. gen., take the initiative in, begin, Hdt.1.5, 4.1, cf. Th.2.74, etc.; And.1.142, cf. Pl.Mx.237b

ὑπαρωματίζω.definition: have something of an aromatic flavour, Dsc.3.8

ὑπασθενέω.definition: to be a little unwell, Phryn.PSp.120B

ὑπασπίδιος.definition: covered with a shield, in Hom. only as Adv., and Il.13.158, 807, 16.609:—after Hom.as Adj., AsiusFr.Ep.13.7 K.; the body-armour and arms of Ajax, S.Aj.1408 ; sleep an armed sleep, sleep in arms, E.Rh.740

ὑπαστράπτω.definition: flash or gleam by reflection, Philostr.VA2.24

ὑπασχολέομαι.definition: to be a subordinate official, OGI179.10

ὑπατεία.definition: the office or rank of consulate

ὑπατεύω.definition: to be consul, Mon.Anc.Gr.11.21, Plu.Publ.3; to be consular governor, Ath.Mitt.48.102, IGRom.1.575 : abs., ib.3.1277

ὑπάτη.definition: the highest of the three strings which formed the framework of the musical scale , but the lowest in pitch, Philol.6, Pl.R.443d, etc.; the highest tetrachord, Anon.Oxy.667.16; . . raising of pitch from the low notes, …

ὑπατοειδής.definition: in the region of the in Music, Aristid. Quint.1.12; Bacch.Harm.43

ὑπαυγάζω.definition: shine under, gleam beneath; begin to shine, dawn, of daybreak, Luc.VH2.47, Polyaen.7.8.2

ὑπαυλέω.definition: play on the flute in accompaniment, Alcm.78; D.C.74.5; Posidon.4J.; Luc.Harm.1: abs., Id.Salt.83

ὑπαφίσταμαι.definition: step back, withdraw, Antipho4.4.1; Men.Sam.153; Thales ap.D.L.1.44; Ael.NA2.25

ὕπαφρος.definition: frothy, Sch.BT Il.14.16; = Heraclid.Tarent. ap. Erot., who cites Hp.de Arte10, S.Frr.236, 312; so in E.Rh.711 , acc. to Sch.; Hsch. explains by also and . codd. Hp., E., Hsch., Phot.; codd.Erot.; in Hp. this sense har…

ὑπαχλύνομαι.definition: Pass., grow dark by degrees, Q.S.1.67

ὑπεγείρω.definition: rouse gradually, Philostr.VS1.21.5; Id.Im.1.24, cf. Ael.NA6.1

ὑπέγκειμαι.definition: form an inner layer, cj. for in Sor.1.57

ὑπεγκλίνω.definition: turn a little or gradually, Orph.A.1205

ὑπείκω.definition: Ep. with impf. Il.16.305; yield, give way, Id.An.7.7.31: abs., of a seaman, . . S.Ant.716; of things, Il.20.266; S.Ant.713; X.Eq.7.6; are soft and yielding, Id.Cyr.8.8.16; in a yielding substance, Arist.PA694b15; . . …

ὑπειλέομαι.definition: Pass., wriggle, creep under, Ael.NA9.57; glossed by Hp. ap. Gal.19.148; of a bandage, to be passed under, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.51.1

ὕπειμι.definition: to be under, c. dat; to be or lie underneath, Id.2.127; X.An.3.4.7; if we had not some solid support, basis, Phld.D.3.11: metaph., A.Pers.815 codd

ὑπεισβαίνω.definition: steal into, cj. Housman in E.Med.382

ὑπεισδύομαι.definition: Med. with aor. 2 Act. get in secretly, slip or steal in, Hdt.1.12 ; come or go in gradually, Arist.GC325b4:—Act. pres. EM290.13

ὑπείσειμι.definition: enter upon, succeed to; succeed to an office, ib.5.1677.48

ὑπεισέρχομαι.definition: enter upon secretly; come into one's mind, Luc.Merc.Cond.11

ὑπεκβαίνω.definition: go out from below, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. of a vein, Gal.2.793; escaping . . , Agath.4.28, cf. 5.1,20

ὑπεκβάλλω.definition: cast out, reject, AP5.65; f.l. for in Plu.2.530d

ὑπεκδέχομαι.definition: have under oneself, of a cow, of a calf at the udder, AP9.722

ὑπεκδιδράσκω.definition: only in aor. run out, escape secretly from, Plu.2.642b; Id.Flam.20: abs., D.C.36.24

ὑπεκδύομαι.definition: Med., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., slip out of, escape, c. acc., E.Cyc.347, cf. Plu.2.170f, Opp.H.3.384, etc.: metaph., Phld.Sto.Herc.339.13: also c. gen., Plu.Dem.9: abs., having slipped out, Hdt.1.10, Plu.Arat.9, etc.;…

ὑπέκδυσις.definition: slipping out or away, escape, Opp.H.3.395

ὑπεκθέσιμος.definition: of merchandise, deposited for re- exportation, GDI5040.25 ; cf. II

ὑπεκθέω.definition: run off secretly or gradually, Emp.100.21, Plu.Pomp.80

ὑπεκκαθαίρω.definition: purge from beneath, in Pass., Hp.Mul.1.60, Nat.Mul.35

ὑπεκκαίω.definition: kindle, Thphr.Ign.63: metaph., stir up, Luc.Peregr.26; inflame, Plu.2.616e; Id.Dio22

ὑπεκκαλύπτω.definition: uncover from below or a little, AP7.480

ὑπέκκαυμα.definition: combustible matter, fuel; the supposed Sphere of Fire surrounding the atmosphere, Simp.in Cael.20.26, al

ὑπεκκαύστρια.definition: she who lights a fire underneath, name of the priestess of Athene at Soli, Plu.2.292a Hsch.)

ὑπέκκειμαι.definition: Pass., to be carried out to a place of safety, to be stowed safe away, Hdt.8.41,9.73, Th.8.31; of money, Th.1.137; Isoc.19.18.— cf. I

ὑπεκκλέπτω.definition: carry off secretly, J.AJ14.11.6, Opp.H.4.48:—Pass., Plu.Them.25

ὑπεκκλίνω.definition: bend aside, escape, Ar.Eq.272 : c. acc., shun, avoid, Plu.Cam.18

ὑπεκκομίζω.definition: carry out or away to safety, Th.4.123, Plu.Cam.21; eliminate insensibly, Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.51:—Med., get all one's goods carried out to safety, Hdt.9.6, cf. X.Cyr.2.4.13

ὑπεκκρίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be carried off insensibly, D.L.9.76

ὑπεκλείπω.definition: fail or flag by degrees, Thphr.Ign.55, Gal.8.489

ὑπεκλύω.definition: loosen or weaken a little, Plu.Nic.14; J.BJ7.8.5; Sor.2.61 ; Ps.-Dsc.1.103; Sch.Il.6.260; weaken the force of, A.D.Synt.224.4:—Pass., cease, become weaker and weaker, Hp.Mul.1.25; Sch.Ar.V.151; S.E.M.11.214, cf. Sor.2…

ὑπεκπέμπω.definition: send out secretly, Th.4.8; E.Hec.6; Id.Andr.47:—Pass., c. acc. loci, to Phocis, S.El.1350

ὑπεκπεράω.definition: go forth and pass over, Q.S.5.246, cf. Orph.A.69

ὑπεκπίπτω.definition: miss, J.AJ16.11.5; prolapse, cj. in Sor.1.12

ὑπεκπνέω.definition: exhale or evaporate gradually, metaph., Pl.Ax.365c

ὑπεκπονέω.definition: work out under another's command, Poll.9.110

ὑπεκπροθέω.definition: run forth from under, outstrip, . . Il.9.506: abs., . . running on before, 21.604, cf. Od.8.125, A.R.4.937

ὑπεκπροθρῴσκω.definition: aor. part. spring out from under, Opp.C.4.160

ὑπεκπρολύω.definition: loose from under, loosed the mules from under the carriage-yoke, unyoked and let them go to graze, Od.6.88

ὑπεκπρορέω.definition: flow up and out, of water running in and out of a rock-basin, ib.87

ὑπεκπροφεύγω.definition: flee away secretly, escape and flee, Il.20.147, 21.44; Od.20.43: c. acc., . . 12.113; Hes.Sc.42

ὑπεκπροχέομαι.definition: Pass., stream forth from under, Q.S.13.57

ὑπεκρέω.definition: flow out from under, Philostr.Im.1.12; metaph., pass away gradually, Pl.Smp.203e; opp. Arist.GC321b27, Plot.4.4.42; c. acc., Plu.Mar.46; of a person, having slipped out of the tent, Id.Pomp.3

ὑπεκρήγνυμαι.definition: Pass., to be gradually broken away, Plu.Cam.3

ὑπεκρίπτω.definition: dislodge by intrigue, 'elbow out of . . ' Id.Comp.Ages.Pomp.1

ὑπεκσῴζω.definition: save by drawing away from, A.Pers.453: abs., Il.23.292

ὑπεκτήκω.definition: cause to waste slowly away, Gal.13.745; ib.242; Heras ap.eund.13.795:—Pass., Hp.Flat.12

ὑπεκτίθεμαι.definition: Med., bring one's property to a place of; deposit for re-exportation, . . GDI5040.21; cf

ὑπεκτρέπω.definition: turn gradually or secretly from a thing, S.Tr.549:—Med., turn aside from, c. acc., Pl.Phd.108b: c. inf., decline the task of helping . . , S.OC566

ὑπεκτρέχω.definition: fut. Id.Ant.1086: aor; run out beyond, S.Tr.167

ὑπεκτροφή.definition: upbringing of a succession, v.l. for in E.Fr.282.6

ὑπεκτρώγω.definition: aor. 2 gnaw secretly away, Macho ap.Ath.13.579d

ὑπεκφέρω.definition: carry out a little, lifted; carry out from under, carry off, so as to be out of danger, 5.318; 15.628: generally, carry away, bear onward, Od.3.496; Plu.Luc.17; A.R.1.1264

ὑπεκφύομαι.definition: Pass., grow gradually out of, Philostr.Im.1.15

ὑπεκχαλάω.definition: let oneself down from; Pass., to be relaxed, Sor.1.65

ὑπεκχέω.definition: in Pass., well up, A.R.3.705: metaph. in Act., get rid of, Plu.2.78e

ὑπεκχωρέω.definition: withdraw, retire; to be purged, Hp.Loc.Hom.33

ὑπελαύνω.definition: ride up so as to meet; Pass., to be purged downwards, Aret.CA1.5

ὑπελίσσω.definition: turn up, Ach.Tat.1.6:—Pass., 3sg. pf. written is wrapped up, BGU781i10, vi6

ὑπεμπίπρημι.definition: put fire under, set on fire, J.BJ2.19.4, D.C.62.16

ὑπεμφαίνω.definition: hint at, indicate, S.E.M.1.4, Gal.19.556; intr., to be cogent, of a proof, Papp.650.5

ὑπεναντιόομαι.definition: Pass., to be opposed or opposite, Arist.EE1240a12, Phgn.807a26

ὑπεναντίωσις.definition: opposition, like Hp.Aph.2.22, Loc.Hom.44, Arist.SE173a28, A.D.Conj.251.2; involving contrarieties, D.61.14; Arist.de An.409b22; Longin.10.3

ὑπενδίδωμι.definition: give way a little, Th.2.64, Ph.1.456; c. dat., Id.2.10; of the legs, Sor.1.113

ὑπενδύω.definition: put on underneath, Alex.98.11 :—Med., Demoph.Sim.31:—Pass., having tunics on under, Plu.Aem.18, cf. Id.2.595e

ὑπένειμι.definition: to be in down below, Epigr.Gr.238

ὑπεννοέω.definition: have in mind, secretly purpose, Ael.VH4.8

ὑπεξάγω.definition: carry out from under or secretly, esp; in Medic. sense, carry off, Hp.Loc.Hom.30, cf. Aret.CA2.6; relax the bowels, Plu.2.635b; Artem.1.67

ὑπεξαιρετέος.definition: to be removed, Hp.Mul.1.11; one must remove, Ph.1.362, 399, 521

ὑπεξαιρέω.definition: take away from below or gradually; make away with, destroy secretly or gradually, Pl.R.567b; E.Hipp.633; set him quit of all danger, Th.4.83; , and even if he fears [thus] to do away with the accusation, let him give …

ὑπεξαίρω.definition: subtract, HeroGeom.10.4, al; Pass., to be elated, Arist.VV1251b19

ὑπεξανάγομαι.definition: Pass., put out to sea secretly, Th.3.74

ὑπεξαναδύομαι.definition: Med., with aor. 2 dive out and emerge, come from under secretly or gradually, Il.13.352; duck or stoop so as to avoid a blow, Theoc.22.123

ὑπεξανίσταμαι.definition: aor. 2 arise, Plu.Cam.22, cf. Luc.Merc.Cond.39; rise as a mark of respect for . . , Id.Demon.63, Plu.Lyc.20, etc

ὑπεξαντλέω.definition: drain out from below, exhaust, . . E.Ion927

ὑπεξάπτω.definition: kindle secretly or gradually, Ael.NA14.20:—Pass., Id.VH14.41

ὑπεξαφύομαι.definition: Pass., to be drained off, of streams that lose themselves in the sand, A.R.2.983

ὑπέξειμι.definition: withdraw gradually, Hdt.4.120; go out to meet or against one, Hdt.1.176 codd

ὑπεξελαύνω.definition: drive away secretly or gradually, Hdt.4.120 : intr., march away, ib.130

ὑπεξερύω.definition: drag out and away, Hdt.7.225:— Med., . . A.R.2.1181

ὑπεξέρχομαι.definition: aor. 2 pf. out from; rise up and quit one's domicile, emigrate, . . Hdt.1.73, 8.36

ὑπεξέχω.definition: intr., withdraw or retire secretly, Hdt.5.72; Id.8.132; Id.6.74

ὑπεξίστημι.definition: alter gradually, Hsch.; esp. for the; Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., withdraw from, Luc.Am.17; Plu.Cat.Mi.19; Id.CG1; give up all claim to it, Hdt.3.83: c. inf., Luc.Sat.6

ὑπεξούσιος.definition: but POxy. , subject to the power of another, opp. Cod.Just.6.4.4.25, Sch.E.Andr.411,628; POxy.129.2 , cf. Mich.in EN45.33; = filius familias, Gloss

ὑπεράγαμαι.definition: to be exceedingly pleased; admire above measure, for a thing, Luc.Dem.Enc.33; Ael.VH12.1

ὑπεραγανακτέω.definition: to be exceedingly angry or vexed at, Pl.R.535e; Aeschin.1.60, cf. Thphr. ap. Porph.Abst.2.29: abs., Arist.Fr.163, Ael.VH8.9

ὑπεραγαπάω.definition: love exceedingly, make much of, c. acc., D.23.196, Arist.EN1168a1; for a thing, J.AJ12.4.6

ὑπεράγω.definition: excel, surpass, c. gen., Plb.11.13.5; D.S.3.35: c. acc., Hp.Ep.27: mostly in part. eminent, principal, SIG588.67 ; extravagant, excessive, Phld.Herc.1251.5; extraordinary, D.S.13.90, etc.; Id.5.17, etc.; c. acc., v.l.…

ὑπεραγωνιάω.definition: to be in great distress, D.61.28; Pl.Euthd.300c; for one, J.AJ16.4.1, Hierocl.in CA13p.448M

ὑπεραγωνίζομαι.definition: Med., fight for, J.BJ2.12.7, App.BC1.96, Jul.Or.2.55c; Them.Or.2.37a

ὑπεραείρω.definition: = aor. was uplifted beyond measure, AP5.298

ὑπεραιδέομαι.definition: feel great shame before, stand in great awe of, c. acc., A.R.3.978

ὑπεραιμέω.definition: have over- much blood, X.Eq.4.2: v

ὑπεραίρω.definition: lift or raise up over; heighten, Philostr.VA3.35

ὑπεραισχύνομαι.definition: Pass., feel much ashamed, . . Aeschin.3.151; Id.1.33: c. part., to be ashamed at doing a thing, Dromo1

ὑπεραιωρέω.definition: suspend or support above; hold up, raise, Aret.CD1.3:—Pass., of the overlapping end of a dislocated bone, to be lifted or drawn over, Hp.Art.70; ib.71, Fract.14, cf. 41: abs., Id.Art.22: Littré gives the Act. in same …

ὑπερακμάζω.definition: surpass in vigour or bloom, Myro2 J.: abs., PSI6.666.18

ὑπερακοντίζω.definition: overshoot, i. e. outdo, Ar.Av.363 ; I overshot him with my 200 kine, Id.Eq.659, cf. Diph.66.5; also has outdone them in stealing, Ar.Pl.666:—Pass., has been made to excel . . , Alex.Aphr.Pr.2Prooem

ὑπερακούω.definition: pf. hear exceedingly well, Phryn.PSp.121 B

ὑπερακρίζω.definition: mount and climb over, c. acc; project, beetle over, c. gen., E.Supp.988

ὑπεράλγεινος.definition: in excessive anguish, f. l. in Aristid.Or.48.63

ὑπεραλγέω.definition: feel pain for or because of; grieve exceedingly, at a thing, Hdt.2.129, Arist.Rh.1380b33; Luc.Asin.38: abs., E.Med.118 ; Arist.Rh.1383b33; in mind, E.Heracl.619

ὑπεράλλομαι.definition: spring or leap over, or beyond, c. gen; metaph., leap to a high place, LXXSi.38.33

ὑπεραμπέχω.definition: cover all in its embrace, Tim.Fr.8

ὑπεραναβαίνω.definition: pass over, cross, Zos.2.53; rise above, Gal.19.172

ὑπεραναιδεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be surpassed in impudence, Ar.Eq.1206 ; Dind. suggests citing AB80

ὑπερανάκειμαι.definition: Pass., lie above another at table, D.L.7.17 codd

ὑπεραναλίσκω.definition: also overspend, exceed estimate, PCair. Zen.702.17, al. , PHib.1.100.1 , Sammelb.7451.65 :—Pass., PCair.Zen.176.2 ; Supp.Epigr.4.447.60

ὑπερανέχω.definition: rise up over, Eust.1020.28; excel; hold above, Conon49.2

ὑπερανθέω.definition: bloom exceedingly, Arat.1060, Poll.3.71; to be over-prosperous, D.C.Fr.39.3

ὑπερανίεμαι.definition: to be excessively diluted, Crito ap.Gal.13.880

ὑπερανίσταμαι.definition: Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., stand up or project over, c. gen., D.H.1.15, 9.68: abs., Id.3.68, Luc.Icar.12: metaph., strutting, conceited, Philostr.Her.15

ὑπεραντλέομαι.definition: Pass., to be very leaky, to be water-logged, Luc.Merc.Cond.2

ὑπέραντλος.definition: prop. of a ship, full of water; of persons, Diph.43.12: metaph., over-charged, Luc.Tim.18; E.Hipp.767 ; Plu.Mar.45

ὑπεράνω.definition: Adv. above, opp. SIG588.31; excessive repetitions, Plb.12.24.1; but one supreme quality, MenoIatr.14.18

ὑποβορβορύζω.definition: rumble a little, of the bowels, Hp.Epid.4.7, Coac.62,285; Aret.SA2.6, 11

ὑποβρέμω.definition: roar or rumble beneath, A.Pr.433 , cf. Orph.A.1267:—Med., Nic.Al.290

ὑποβρέχω.definition: of a toper, soaks away the rest of the day, Alex.275; AP11.3; somewhat drunk, Men.Inc.2.34, cf. Ph.1.260, Luc.DDeor.23.2:—in sense treat, moisten, prob. cj. in Thphr.HP5.3.3

ὑποβρυχάομαι.definition: roar or bellow a little, Luc.Am.6, Tryph.319, etc.; of the breathing of one in a passion, Adam.2.41

ὑποβύθιος.definition: under the depths, gloss on Erot

ὑποβώμιον.definition: Dim. of sq., Inscr.Grecques et Latines de la Syrie 1.153

ὑποβωμίς.definition: base of an altar, Jahresh.18 Beibl.23

ὑπογάμιον.definition: illicit intercourse with a betrothed person, Ph.2.311

ὑπογάστριον.definition: the lower belly from the navel; the belly of a sea-fish, esp. of the tunny, a favourite dish at Athens, Stratt.4,31 , Ar.Fr.364, etc.; whence the joke in Id.V.195

ὑπογελάω.definition: laugh a little, smile, Pl.Chrm.162b, Polem.Phgn.19

ὑπογενειάζω.definition: entreat by touching the chin, Aeschin.1.61

ὑπογενειάσκω.definition: to have a beard beginning to grow, Hdn.Philet.p.444P

ὑπογένειον.definition: the part under the chin, Eust.548.3

ὑπογεωργέω.definition: farm as in Pass., prob. in Sammelb.7193viii 12

ὑπογεωργός.definition: sub-lessee and farmer of state land, POxy.1661.4,7

ὑπογίγνομαι.definition: Ion. and later Gr. grow up after or in succession, Il.11.417; Hdt.3.159; of inflammation following a hurt, Hp.Art.38, cf. Ti.Locr.104a; of feelings and thoughts, Plb.2.44.1, 6.6.7, etc

ὑπογκόομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat swollen, Poll.3.49, 4.68

ὑπόγλαυκος.definition: somewhat grey, of eyes, X.Cyn.5.23; of leaves, Dsc.2.180,4.60

ὑπογλαύσσω.definition: glance from under, glance furtively, like of the eyes, Call.Dian.54, Mosch.2.86

ὑπογλυκαίνω.definition: sweeten a little: metaph., coax and smooth down, Ar.Eq.216

ὑπογλώσσιος.definition: Subst., the region under the tongue, Arist.HA506a28, Heliod. ap. Orib.45.6.5

ὑπογλωσσίς.definition: Att. swelling on the; the under surface of the tongue, Poll.2.105, Hsch

ὑπόγλωσσος.definition: somewhat talkative, Polem.Phgn.35; under the tongue, Poet.de herb.46

ὑπογογγύζω.definition: murmur or mutter to oneself, Sch.D.19.197, Dosith.p.430 K

ὑπογραμματεύω.definition: serve as under-secretary, Antipho6.49; Lys.30.29, cf. D.19.70

ὑπογραφεύς.definition: one who writes under another's; person who has drafted or signed a deed on behalf of another, PAmh.2.110.24 , cf. PMeyer 13.17 , etc.; PMasp.23.10

ὑπογραφίς.definition: pencil, Poll.7.128; a surgical instrument, Id.4.181, 10.149

ὑποδάκνω.definition: bite privily, App.BC1.101; to be somewhat pungent, Dsc.4.142: metaph., to be mordant, Demetr.Eloc.260

ὑποδακρύω.definition: weep a little or secretly, Luc.DDeor.6.2; ooze, of blood, Antyll. ap. Orib.7.21.8

ὑποδαμνάω.definition: master or weaken beneath one, Il.21.270:—Pass. , to be overcome, overpowered, Od.3.214, 16.95; aor. 1 part. of a woman, subdued by a man, yielding to his embrace, h.Hom.17.4, Hes.Sc.53, Th.327,374; also of a man, subd…

ὑπόδειγμα.definition: sign, token, indication, v.l. in; illustration, picture showing how something is to be done, Apollon.Cit.2,3

ὑποδείδω.definition: trans., shrink in fear under, cower before, c. acc., Hom., who uses mostly the aor. , Il.1.406, 12.413, al.; Od.2.66: Ep. pf. 2 and plpf., 17.564, Philet.8, Il.5.521: Ep. pf. 1 h.Merc.165: literally, of birds, cower b…

ὑποδείκνυμι.definition: abs., indicate one's will, intimate, X.Mem.4.3.13, cf. An.5.7.12; warn, Ev.Matt.3.7

ὑποδεικτέος.definition: to be pointed out, Id.3.36.5; one must point out, indicate, Sor.1.53, S.E.M.7.167, Aët.9.38

ὑποδείκτης.definition: one who points out, Sm.Ps.83.7, Gloss

ὑποδειλιάω.definition: to be somewhat cowardly; = f.l. for Plb.35.3.4

ὑποδειμαίνω.definition: = stand in secret awe of, Hdt.7.104, cf. Plu.2.986d

ὑποδειπνέω.definition: dine as a substitute for another, Luc.Gall.10

ὑποδέκτης.definition: receiver, steward, a financial official, = PLips.ap. Wilcken Chr.43 intr. ; Stud.Pal.20.87.1, 91.1 : abs., POxy.136.15 , PLond.5.1667.1 , Just.Nov.163.2, etc

ὑποδελεάζω.definition: dub. l. in Ph.Bel.100.39 codd.: cj. Diels

ὑποδέμω.definition: lay as a foundation, Hdt.2.127:—Med., found, Str.7Fr.35

ὑποδερίς.definition: the lower part of the neck

ὑποδέρω.definition: strip off the skin a little or below, Gal.2.700, 18.103, Orib.46.15.5

ὑποδεσίδιον.definition: Dim. of sq. II.2, = soccus, Gloss

ὑπόδεσις.definition: under-bandaging, Hp.Off.11; putting on one's shoes, Arist.Pol.1257a9, Cael.271a33, Luc.Gall.26

ὑποδεσμέω.definition: = foreg., in Med., Sch.A.R.4.1515: abs., Sch.S.Tr.779

ὑποδέχομαι.definition: in Ion. and Dor. Prose Hdt. (v; entertain to a meal, Antipho1.18, cf. IG4.679.15 ; Th.6.22; the host , Epict.Fr.17; D.S.17.115, cf. Plu.Alex.23

ὑποδέω.definition: late Gr. Gloss., Dosith.p.435; esp. underbind the feet, i. e. shoe, because the ancient sandals or shoes were bound on with straps, Arist.HA499a29, cf. Plu.Pomp.24, Paus.10.25.4; so Cobet restores for in Pl.Prt.321b:—…

ὑποδηλόω.definition: show privately, Ar.Th.1011; hint at, suggest, Philostr.Her.Prooem.3; Plu.Nic.4; imply, Ael.NA5.45; foreshadow, ib.7.7

ὑποδήλωσις.definition: insinuation, a rhetorical phrase ascribed to Evenus of Paros in Pl.Phdr.267a, cf. Poll.4.33

ὑπόδημα.definition: sole bound under the foot with straps, sandal, . . Od.15.369; . . 18.361, cf. Hdt.1.195, etc.; Pl.Alc.1.128a, etc.; whereas is a shoe or half-boot, which covered the whole foot ; is sts. used alone in this sense, cf. …

ὑποδημάτιον.definition: Dim. of Hp.Art.62; of the shoes of an ass, Arr.Epict.4.1.80

ὑποδηματουργός.definition: sandalmaker, JHS22.124 , prob. in Wiener Denkschr.44.27 No.59

ὑποδῃόομαι.definition: Pass., to be treated in hostile manner, Q.S.2.260, 3.355

ὑποδιαβιβρώσκομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat corroded, Hp.Cord.6

ὑποδιαίρεσις.definition: subdivision, Diog.Bab.Stoic.3.215, Gal.14.689, Hermog.Inv.3.10, S.E.M.11.15, Vett.Val.98.10, Procl.Hyp.3.10, etc

ὑποδιακονέω.definition: serve under another, CIG1947.8 :—Med., Poll.4.92, cf. Arg.Theoc.2

ὑποδιαλείπω.definition: intermit a little, of the pulse, Gal.8.487

ὑποδιανοέομαι.definition: Med., design secretly, v.l. in Jul.Ep.107

ὑποδιαπήγνυμαι.definition: Pass., with pf. 2 to be fixed across below, Ph.Bel.74.11

ὑποδιαστολή.definition: slight stop, between words in speaking; mark to divide words from one another , e. g. to distinguish it from Ps.-D.T.674, Sch.D.T.p.24H., al., Eust.701.56, 1465.16

ὑποδίδωμι.definition: intr., give way, Arist.MA698b15; Aristid.Or.31.12, Philostr.VA3.20; of power and empire, decay, Aristid.2.187 J., Philostr.VS1.21.4; in strength, Id.Gym.48

ὑποδιπλάσιος.definition: the inverse of double, i. e. 1/2, Nicom.Ar.1.18

ὑποδιπλόω.definition: = duplico, Gloss.:—Pass., to be folded double, Gal.UP4.11

ὑποδίψιος.definition: exciting thirst in some degree, Man.5.188

ὑποδομή.definition: Dor. supporting wall, = II, IG4.823.36 , 11.146 A72 , 158 A72 , al

ὑποδορά.definition: gradual stripping of the skin, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.15.5, Antyll.ib.45.25.5, Aët.15.8

ὑποδοχεῖον.definition: reservoir, Aristeas89,91, PTeb.733.8 ; used for storage of fish, PHamb.6.10 ; of wine, PSI8.918.2 , POxy.729.28 ; PPetr.2p.64 ; coupled with PSI9.1056.6 ; perh. also, store-house, barn, BGU301.11 , cf. PTeb.86.15, al.…

ὑποδοχεύς.definition: receiver, host, Luc.Fug.30, Charito3.2, Phot. s.v. Astrol., of a planet entertaining another, Vett.Val.103.1

ὑποδοχή.definition: entertainment, hospitality, Ar.Pax530 , Pl.Lg.919a ; . . Hdt.7.119; . . E.IA1229; Ath.5.210e; SIG1107.12 ; also for the reception of the army , Th.7.74

ὑποδράσσομαι.definition: Att. Med., try to get hold of, Plu.Caes.14 codd

ὑποδράω.definition: Ep. serve, c. dat., Od.15.333; Ael.NA9.33

ὑποδρομή.definition: running under or into the way of a thing; place to run down into, burrow, Ael.NA16.15; bower, Id.VH3.1

ὑπόδρομος.definition: name for a venomous spider, = Ael.NA6.26; = IV, a place for ships to run into, cove, Ph.1.14, al., Ptol.Geog.4.6.2

ὑποδυσφορέω.definition: to be somewhat restless or impatient, Pl.Ep.357e

ὑποδυσωπέομαι.definition: Pass., look somewhat askance at, Plu.2.646b

ὑποδυτήριον.definition: in pl., coves, places for ships to run into, Str.14.5.6

ὑποδύτης.definition: garment worn under a coat of mail, PEnteux.32.6 , D.S.17.44, Plu.Phil.11; simply undergarment, LXXEx.28.31, IG5.1390.20 , J.BJ5.5.7

ὑποδύω.definition: metaph., undergo danger, Id.3.69; intr., slip in under, Id.4.75: c. acc., slip into, insinuate oneself into, Id.6.2; Phld.Lib.p.64 O.: v. infr. II.1d

ὑποδώριος.definition: hypo-Dorian, Ath.14.625a; Plu.2.1142f:—Adv. in the hypo-Dorian mode, Arist.Pr.920a8, 922b10

ὑποεπιμερής.definition: = Ph.2.183 cod. M, cf. Iamb.in Nic.p.37 P

ὑποζεύγνυμι.definition: pf. Orus ap.EM786.5:—yoke under; metaph., subjugate, Orus l. c.:—Pass., submit to, S.Aj.24

ὑποζέω.definition: ferment a little, begin to ferment, Gp.6.12.2

ὑποζητέω.definition: search for, dub. in BGU1024 iv 21

ὑποζύγιον.definition: beast for the yoke, beast of; later specifically an ass, LXXZa.9.9, Ev.Matt.21.5, 2 Ep.Pet.2.16; PCair.Zen.158, ; PPetr.3p.56 ; Hp.Aph.4.70

ὑποζυγόω.definition: = Med., bring under one's power, Luc.Am.28:—Pass., Hp.Art.30

ὑποζυμόομαι.definition: Pass., ferment slightly, Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.5.1

ὑποζώννυμι.definition: brace a ship, so as to make her seaworthy , IG l. c., Plb. l. c., Act.Ap.27.17; IG22.1621.68

ὑποθάλπω.definition: light or kindle secretly, Ael.Fr.306:—Pass., glow under, AP12.92

ὑποθειάζω.definition: to be divinely inspired, Philostr.VA1.3, cf. 6.11

ὑποθεραπεύω.definition: to be disposed to worship, Philostr.VA4.40; bribe, Memn.24

ὑποθερμαίνω.definition: heat a little, Gal.11.417:—Pass., grow somewhat hot, Il.16.333, 20.476, cf. Hp.Ulc.26: metaph., Luc.DMeretr.8.3

ὑπόθερμος.definition: somewhat hot, Gal.6.240, Poll.5.108: of persons, somewhat hot or passionate, Hdt.6.38, cf. Luc.Cal.5; of a horse, Poll.1.192; Plu.2.1146f

ὑποθέτης.definition: one who suggests, prompter, adviser, Anon. ap. Suid

ὑπόθετος.definition: placed under: Medic., suppository, pessary, Antiph.208, Alex.Trall.9.3

ὑποθέω.definition: fut. make a secret attack; cut in before, in running a race, supplant, Ar.Eq.1161; of a solar eclipse, . . Cleom.2.3; Them.Or.26.317b

ὑποθεωρέω.definition: hold up and look at, Plu.2.42c

ὑποθήγω.definition: whet, Ael.NA5.45; sharpen, make acute, ib.9.16; stimulate, ib.5.39: metaph., provoke him to rise, ib.8.2:—Pass., Id.Fr.81

ὑποθηκάριος.definition: of or for a mortgage, Just.Nov.4.2, Procop.Arc.28: in Lat. form hypothecarius, Cod.Just.4.32.26, al

ὑποθήκη.definition: suggestion, counsel, warning; pledge, deposit, mortgage, D.34.50, Arist.Oec.1348b21, Supp.Epigr.1.366.39 , PCair.Zen.504.4 , PEnteux.15.4 , etc.; PRein.18.11 ; upon securities given, SIG742.39, cf. 51 , al.; mortgages…

ὑποθηκιμαῖος.definition: relating to a mortgage, PMasp.23.11 , 96.15 ; = fiduciarius, Gloss.: neut. pledge, PMasp.96.38

ὑπόθλασμα.definition: fragment, splinter of bone, v.l. for in Hippiatr.104

ὑποθλίβω.definition: press under or gently, Nic.Th.296 codd. , Al.30, Dsc.1.43, Luc.VH2.14, Cass.Pr.28

ὑποθορυβέω.definition: begin to make a clamour, Th.4.28

ὑποθρύπτομαι.definition: Pass., to be nerveless or emasculated; I wantoned with her face—by stealing kisses, AP5.293.15

ὑποθυμίασις.definition: Ion. fumigation, Hp.Nat.Mul.103 , Dsc.1.67, Sor.2.33, Hippiatr.22

ὑποθυμιάω.definition: fumigate, Luc.DMeretr.4.5:—Med; abs. in Act., make a thick smoke, Aen.Tact.32.1

ὑποθωπεύω.definition: win by flattery, Ar.Ach.639 , V.610 , D.H.7.34, Philostr.VS1.21.4: abs., without using any flattery, Hdt.1.30; Chor.3.84p.69 F.-R

ὑποθωρήσσομαι.definition: Med., arm oneself in secret, Il.18.513

ὑποθωΰσσω.definition: call to a person softly, Ael.NA8.2

ὑποϊάχω.definition: sound forth a little or in answer, AP9.314

ὑποίγνυμι.definition: open a little or secretly, Ar.Th.424, cf. Ec.15

ὑποιδέω.definition: intr., swell up somewhat, Id.Coac.136 , Superf.17, Ael.VH14.7, Philostr.VA3.46, etc

ὑποικίζομαι.definition: in aor. 1 Med., = foreg. I, AP7.372

ὑποικοδομέω.definition: build under, IG 22.463.114; f. l. for Luc.Hist.Conscr.3

ὑποικουρέω.definition: keep house, stay at home, Ael.NA11.32; trans., engage in or plot underhand, . . Ar.Th.1168, cf. Plu.Pomp.42:—Pass., anger secretly cherished, Plb.4.49.4, cf. 3.11.3: the plot, intrigue, Ph.2.202

ὕποινος.definition: under the influence of wine; full of wine, Philostr.Im.1.31; ib.18

ὑποΐσχομαι.definition: Med., catch by holding under, A.R.4.473; ib.169

ὑποκαθαίρω.definition: purge downwards, Hp.Aph.7.68, cf. Thphr.HP7.12.3, Plu.2.127c, Gal.6.248

ὑποκαθέζομαι.definition: lie in ambush, Anon. ap. Suid., Onos.6.7; late aor. sink, settle down, Sch.Th.3.89, Gp.6.18

ὑποκάθημαι.definition: Ion. prop. pf. of; sit below, Philostr.VA3.16; to be placed under, ib.8

ὑποκαθίζω.definition: place in ambush; intr. in Act., lie in ambush, Plb.12.4.14, etc

ὑποκαθίημι.definition: let down by degrees, i. e; Med., leave behind at large, leave untouched, Plb.23.108

ὑποκαθίσταμαι.definition: Pass., settle at the bottom, of; subside, of symptoms, Aret.CA1.1

ὑποκαίω.definition: Att. burn by applying fire below; light under, Luc.Phal.1.11:—Pass., Arist.Mete.355a17

ὑποκάμπτω.definition: bend short back, they; intr., turn back, double as a hare, X.Cyn.5.16

ὑποκαπνίζω.definition: burn for purpose of fumigation, Hp.Mul.2.117, cf. Gal.14.551

ὑποκάπνισμα.definition: that with which one fumigates, Alex. Trall.5.4

ὑποκαπνισμός.definition: fumigation, Dsc.Eup.1.210, Antyll. ap. Orib.8.12.1, Sor.2.33, Gal.16.147

ὑποκαρόω.definition: reduce to a state of stupor, Dsc.Eup.1.26:—Pass., Dsc.4.75

ὑποκάρφω.definition: dry a little or gradually, Nic.Al.80

ὑποκαταβαίνω.definition: descend by degrees, Hdt.2.15; go back gradually, i. e. relax severity of régime, Hp.Aph.1.7

ὑποκατάβασις.definition: gradual descent, Eust.1402.16; glossed by Phot., Suid.; reduction, Gal.17.378

ὑποκαταγελάω.definition: laugh in one's sleeve at, Arr.Epict.4.6.21

ὑποκατακλίνω.definition: lay down under:—Pass., lie down; Pass. also, lie or sit lower at table, ib.618e; J.AJ12.4.9

ὑποκατάκλισις.definition: metaph., taking a lower place, compliance, servility, Plu.2.58c ; a humiliation, Hld.10.25

ὑποκαταπίπτω.definition: sink down under, Ep. aor. Q.S.1.588

ὑποκατασκευάζω.definition: prepare secretly, J.AJ15.4.2; ib.16.1.2 ; prepare beforehand, Iamb.Myst.3.27 ; should be somewhat more studied, Demetr.Eloc.224

ὑποκαταφρονέω.definition: apptly., to be a little irrational, of; despise a little, Aristox.Harm.p.31 M

ὑποκαταχέω.definition: pour gently forth, Alc.39; but pours forth from beneath his wings , is prob. cj

ὑποκάτειμι.definition: go down: further on, lower in the text, AB156, Syn.Alch.p.59 B., Sever.Clyst.p.32D

ὑποκατεσθίω.definition: devour or consume secretly, gloss on Apollon.Lex

ὑποκάτω.definition: Adv. below, under, c. gen; in Logic, the subordinate genus, opp. Arist.Top.143a21; ib.122a9, al

ὑπόκαυσις.definition: burning underneath, Dieuch. ap; burning of bricks, POxy.2153.12

ὑπόκαυστον.definition: the hot-air space under the sweating- room in a bathing establishment, hypocaust, Plin.Ep.2.17, Stat.Silv.1.5.59

ὑπόκαυστος.definition: heated by a hypocaust, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.112

ὑποκαύστρα.definition: the hot-air space of a hypocaust, Gloss.: written three times in PMag.Berol.2.48, al

ὑπόκειμαι.definition: used as Pass. of fut; of places, lie close to, Isoc.4.108; Aeschin.3.118; Plu.Crass.29; Arist.Mete.364a7, cf.Pr.941b39; Gp.2.5.1; the adjacent soil, D.S.3.50; the adjacent country, ibid. ; Plb.5.59.4 codd. ; Id.3.74.2…

ὑποκείρω.definition: cut off, take away, Ph.1.327; metaph., tear, mangle them, Plu.2.829a

ὑποκελεύω.definition: do the duty of a boatswain, give the time in rowing, Luc.Cat.19:—hence Sch. ad loc

ὑπόκενος.definition: somewhat hollow, Ruf.Onom.139, v.l. in Dsc.2.131; simply, hollow, PMag.Par.1.2361; somewhat flabby, Mnesith. ap. Orib.inc.15.8: metaph., Hsch. s.v. ; Hermog.Id.2.9; Hierocl.in CA23p.470 M

ὑποκενόω.definition: empty below, purge, Hp.Prog.23; carry off by purging, Id.Int.20

ὑποκηρύσσω.definition: proclaim by herald, c. inf. fut., PRev.Laws53.18 , cf. AB312:—Med., have a thing proclaimed or cried, esp. for sale, Aeschin.3.41; advertising yourself, Pl.Prt.349a; D.H.9.48: c. acc. et inf., J.AJ3.6.1

ὑποκιθαρίζω.definition: play an accompaniment on the harp, Sch.Il.18.570

ὑποκινδυνεύω.definition: run some risk, f. l. for in Plu.Pel.2

ὑποκινέω.definition: move softly or lightly; metaph., urge gently on, so as to make him speak, Pl.Chrm.162d, Plu.Aem.9; Luc.Eun.13; cf. A.II.2

ὑποκιρσόω.definition: in Pass., of veins, to be swollen, Hp.Ulc.10

ὑποκλάζω.definition: bend the knees under one, sink down, Hld.7.7, Nonn.D.43.47; bow the knee before . . , ib.47.627; Longus3.13 ; Epic. in BKT5 p.85 : metaph. of an expiring lamp, AP5.278 ; of a declining fever, Paul.Aeg.2.47; the mighty…

ὑποκλάω.definition: break underneath; break by degrees, break down, . . Q.S.4.483:—Pass., J.BJ7.8.7; AP5.215

ὑποκλέπτω.definition: steal from under, Dionys.Av.1.11; draw; suffer dishonour by stealth, S.El.114

ὑποκλίνω.definition: bend under or in subjection to; give way to, Herm.in Phdr.p.157 A.: so intr. in Act., . . Orph.A.848

ὑποκλονέομαι.definition: Pass., to be driven in confusion before; to be shaken so as to fall, Q.S.14.572

ὑποκλοπέομαι.definition: Pass., lurk in secret places, Od.22.382

ὑποκλύζω.definition: wash from below; Pass., to be submerged, A.R.1.533 : metaph., to be flooded with mischief, Luc.Nigr.16

ὑποκλυσμός.definition: purging from below, as by a clyster, Plu.2.974c

ὑποκνήθω.definition: scratch a little, Ael. ap. Ar.Byz.Epit.113.6, Tz.H.6.89
